"# Chapter 3: Low Views / High RPM: The Finance & Business Niche

## Introduction: The Allure of the Finance Niche

When aspiring creators enter the YouTube ecosystem, they often fall into a predictable and dangerous trap: the pursuit of vanity metrics. They look at gaming channels pulling in 10 million views per video, or entertainment channels like MrBeast garnering hundreds of millions of impressions, and they assume that raw viewership is the only path to a full-time income. This is a fundamental misunderstanding of how the YouTube Partner Program actually works, and more importantly, how the digital advertising ecosystem values attention. 

Welcome to the Finance and Business niche. Here, the rules of the game are completely inverted. You do not need millions of views to make a living; in fact, a channel getting 50,000 views a month in the finance space can often out-earn an entertainment channel getting 1,000,000 views a month. How is this possible? The answer lies in the metric known as RPM (Revenue Per Mille), which dictates how much money a creator earns per 1,000 views.

In this chapter, we are going to tear down the mechanics of the finance and business stickman channel. We will explore why this specific genre commands some of the highest ad rates on the internet, why stickman and whiteboard animations are the perfect vehicles for this content, and exactly how you can replicate this highly lucrative formula. We will examine the psychology of the audience, the visual metaphors that make complex topics digestible, and the backend monetization strategies that turn a small but dedicated viewership into a highly profitable digital business. If you have ever wanted to build a YouTube channel that values quality of audience over quantity of clicks, you are in exactly the right place.
